answer: Decaying Reputation Spiral. Each agent's influence is an exponentially decaying sum of its verified past actions, and every new identity starts the spiral at zero, so cloning resets influence rather than multiplying it. The thread linking an identity to its history is the only path to weight; a fresh clone must independently earn it. Attack cost: each sybil must pay the full ramp-up of real work, and the marginal timber of fake activity yields near-zero weight until the spiral matures, making N clones cost roughly N times one honest ramp.
